html:
Cholula, in Nahuatl Cholollan, was an ancient city-state on the plain of Puebla in central Mexico, and is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the Americas. It grew up in the same centuries as Teotihuacan and long outlived it. Its people, the Cholulteca, built the Great Pyramid of Cholula in stages over many centuries; by volume it is the largest pyramid in the world.

By the 1400s Cholula was a holy city of the god Quetzalcoatl, a pilgrimage centre and a market famous for fine painted pottery. It sat between the great powers of central Mexico: it often sided with the Aztec Triple Alliance and fought its neighbour Tlaxcala. In October 1519 Hernán Cortés, marching on Tenochtitlan with Tlaxcalan allies, claimed the city was plotting against him and killed thousands of Cholulans in the Cholula massacre. The Spanish later built a church on top of the Great Pyramid, which still stands.
